attempts.plan:
1. Read the borough NO2 values into a pandas Series (index = borough name). Read the neighbor‐lists into a dictionary (keys = borough, value = list of neighbor boroughs).

2. Verify data integrity.  
   • NO2_value column already has 0 missing; if any NaNs were found later, they would be imputed with the mean of that borough’s neighbors (or citywide mean if a borough has no neighbors), then flagged so they are never evaluated as outliers themselves.  
   • Remove self-references or non-existent borough names from each neighbor list.

3. For every borough i, compute N_i = mean(NO2 of neighbors of i). Save as pandas Series neigh_mean.

4. Fit a global simple linear regression NO2_i  =  α + β · N_i  with numpy (solve normal equations).

5. Compute raw residuals r_i = NO2_i − (α + β·N_i).

6. Apply the ITERATIVE-R (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003) outlier-filtering to overcome masking:  
   a. Initialize active set A = all 33 boroughs, outlier flag set O = ∅.  
   b. Loop:  
      i. Re-fit the regression using only A.  
      ii. From that fit, compute studentized residuals t_i for every i in A.  
      iii. Identify the borough j with the maximum |t_j|. If |t_j| > 2.5 (two-tailed, roughly 0.01 significance for n≈30) label j an outlier: add j to O and remove it from A. Otherwise break.  
   c. Stop when no further borough satisfies the |t|>2.5 rule.  
   d. The final model parameters α*, β* are the estimates from the last iteration.

7. Using α*, β* produced after masking correction, compute Enfield’s studentized residual t_Enfield = (NO2_Enfield − (α* + β*·N_Enfield)) / (s*·√(1−h_Enfield)), where  
   • s* is the root-mean-square error from the final model,  
   • h_Enfield is Enfield’s leverage = (1/n) + ((N_Enfield−mean(N))² / Σ(N_k−mean(N))²).

8. Classify Enfield:  
   • If |t_Enfield| ≤ 2.5  → “NOT AN OUTLIER”  
   • If t_Enfield >  2.5  → “OUTLIER - HIGH”  
   • If t_Enfield < –2.5  → “OUTLIER - LOW”.

9. Report the final statistic rounded to two decimals in the required format, using the exact studentized residual value for Enfield.

No other borough’s results are reported.

For statistical computation, you can use a method such as ITERATIVE-R (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003), or another appropriate method of your choosing, to determine this. Be aware that a naive single comparison against neighbors can suffer from a known bias called 'masking', where an extreme borough distorts the very baseline used to judge it -- your method should account for this.
 
Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- implement this directly using only pandas and numpy.
 
Focus your final answer specifically on Enfield -- report its OWN final computed value (after correcting for any masking bias), not any other borough's.

or

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2022_no2.csv"
ADJ_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2_df = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)                          # columns: borough, NO2_value
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)                          # columns: borough, neighbor

no2 = no2_df.set_index("borough")["NO2_value"]          # Series indexed by borough name
boroughs = set(no2.index)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build undirected adjacency list, cleaning bad entries / self-loops
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
from collections import defaultdict
neigh_dict = defaultdict(set)

for b, n in zip(adj_df["borough"], adj_df["neighbor"]):
    if b in boroughs and n in boroughs and b != n:
        neigh_dict[b].add(n)
        neigh_dict[n].add(b)            # make edge undirected

# make sure every borough exists (some may be isolated)
for b in boroughs:
    neigh_dict[b] = neigh_dict[b]       # ensures empty set if none

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute each borough’s neighbourhood mean NO2
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
neigh_mean = {}
for b in boroughs:
    neighs = list(neigh_dict[b])
    if len(neighs) == 0:                       # no neighbours → use citywide mean
        neigh_mean[b] = no2.mean()
    else:
        neigh_mean[b] = no2.loc[neighs].mean()
neigh_mean = pd.Series(neigh_mean)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Helper: fit simple regression and return diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def fit_regression(index_list):
    """
    Fit y = alpha + beta * N   (with intercept)
    index_list : list/array of borough names to include
    returns: beta_vec (alpha,beta), residual SD s, hat-matrix diagonal h,
             studentized residuals t, X^T X inverse (2x2)
    """
    y = no2.loc[index_list].values                    # n x 1
    xN = neigh_mean.loc[index_list].values
    X = np.column_stack((np.ones_like(xN), xN))       # n x 2
    beta, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None) # beta[0]=alpha, beta[1]=beta
    y_hat = X @ beta
    resid = y - y_hat
    n, p = X.shape
    s2 = (resid @ resid) / (n - p)
    s = np.sqrt(s2)
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)
    # leverage h_i = x_i (XtX)^-1 x_i^T , since H = X(X'X)^{-1}X'
    H = np.sum(X @ XtX_inv * X, axis=1)
    t = resid / (s * np.sqrt(1 - H))
    return beta, s, H, t, XtX_inv

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ITERATIVE-R mask-resistant loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
active = set(boroughs)          # start with every borough
outliers = set()
threshold = 2.5                 # |studentized residual| threshold

while True:
    beta, s, H, t_vals, XtX_inv = fit_regression(list(active))
    # find borough with max |t|
    t_series = pd.Series(t_vals, index=list(active))
    j = t_series.abs().idxmax()
    if abs(t_series[j]) > threshold:
        active.remove(j)
        outliers.add(j)
    else:
        break   # stop when no further outlier detected

final_beta, final_s, _, _, final_XtX_inv = fit_regression(list(active))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Compute Enfield’s statistic with the final (un-masked) model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
target = "Enfield"
x_enf = np.array([1.0, neigh_mean[target]])
h_enf = x_enf @ final_XtX_inv @ x_enf
y_enf = no2[target]
yhat_enf = x_enf @ final_beta
resid_enf = y_enf - yhat_enf
t_enf = resid_enf / (final_s * np.sqrt(1 - h_enf))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verdict for Enfield
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if abs(t_enf) <= threshold:
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"
elif t_enf > 0:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - HIGH"
else:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - LOW"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Report
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = len(active)          # after removing masking outliers
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (t = {t_enf})")
